title: Sell Mineral Rights in Semmes, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Semmes, AL | Citronelle Trend
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Semmes, AL on the way to Citronelle? Get a title-researched, no-pressure offer from a direct buyer.
heroLead: Semmes sits west of Mobile on the road toward Citronelle, close enough to Alabama's largest historic oil field that a fair number of families here have held leased or producing mineral interests since the field's mid-century boom.
intro: Farming and timber shaped Semmes for most of its history, and a lot of that same land got swept into leasing activity once the Citronelle Field proved out in the 1950s. Families who farmed here for generations often ended up holding both the surface and the mineral rights on their own land, at least until an operator came through with a lease, and some of those leases have been renewed or extended enough times that they're still active today.

sections.heading: Farmland That Became Producing Acreage
paragraphs: If your family farmed near Semmes and later leased the mineral rights when Citronelle-area drilling expanded, there's a decent chance that lease or a successor to it is still in effect. We check the current status and, where the tract is producing, look at the actual royalty history before pricing an offer.

sections.heading: Confirming What's Still Active
paragraphs: Leases from the original Citronelle boom have been assigned, renewed, and sometimes let lapse over seventy years, so an old family lease near Semmes isn't necessarily the one currently governing your interest. We trace it forward to whoever holds it today before we say anything about what your interest is worth.

faqs.question: Our family's original Citronelle-era lease is decades old. Is it even still valid?
faqs.answer: Possibly, if it's been kept alive by continued production or renewed by the operator. We check the current status before assuming either way.

faqs.question: We're getting a royalty check but don't know which well it's from. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: We can typically identify the well and unit from your check stub or division order, which helps us understand exactly what's driving your payment.

faqs.question: Is Semmes considered part of the Citronelle Field itself?
faqs.answer: It sits close to the trend, though field boundaries are specific. We check whether your exact tract is inside an active unit before pricing anything.

faqs.question: Our family still farms the surface even though the minerals are leased. Does that complicate a sale?
faqs.answer: No, selling your mineral interest doesn't affect your ability to keep farming the surface. The two are separate rights under Alabama law.

faqs.question: How do we find our division order or the current operator's contact information?
faqs.answer: If you don't have a recent statement handy, we can often identify the operator ourselves from the county record and the well's unit designation.
